episodes.169779: During the evening hours, a thunderstorm developed over Petroleum County, eventually reaching severe levels.
episodes.169843: Two people were killed after heavy rain which produced a destructive debris flow in the Cameron Peak burn area.  The 37-yr old woman and her 12-yr old daughter were in a camp trailer that was swept away at Calcite Road along Sheep Creek.  In addition, a cabin along Granite Road was destroyed in the flood. Buckhorn Rd (LCR 44H) was heavily damaged in the flood. Several other roads were washed out or extensively damaged.
episodes.169972: Persistent monsoon moisture fueled scattered showers and thunderstorms across eastern Utah. The stronger storms produced gusty winds up to 58 mph across Grand Valley.
episodes.169975: Ample monsoon moisture paired with the aided support aloft from a passing shortwave resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms across western Colorado. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to a localized debris flows and flash flooding in portions of San Miguel and Mesa counties.
episodes.170100: There were some early afternoon marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.170122: A stationary frontal boundary across central Minnesota, and an increasing very moist airmass with PWATs near 1.75 early Friday morning, July 15th, was the setup for a flash flood event over Chippewa County Wisconsin. During the early morning, several waves of thunderstorms developed across west central, Wisconsin, and east central Minnesota, and drifted southeast across west central Wisconsin for several hours. The upper level flow was conducive for training of the thunderstorms as a strong low level jet at 850H impinged upon very moist airmass. By daybreak, a pocket of 4 to 5 inches of rain fell in Chippewa County where flash flooding was reported. Elsewhere, rainfall totals ranged from 2 to 4 inches from Barron to Chippewa County.
episodes.170204: Showers and thunderstorm developed north of a warm front during the morning hours on Friday (7/15) across portions of central Wisconsin.  A total of 2 to 4 inches of rain fell in a short period across Wood County, causing flash flooding.
episodes.170360: Upper-level ridging persisted across the Desert Southwest and Southern Plains, extending north to over the Central and Northern CONUS plains. A subtle wave lifting northeast from the Great Basin toward the Northern Rockies provided widespread lift, combined with a steepening lapse rate and weak to moderate instability to support development of scattered thunderstorms across Southwest and Central Montana. Primary threat was damaging, gusty winds. SPC had much of the CWA under a Marginal Risk with a portion of the CWA under a Slight Risk for severe storms on the 14-15th, General Thunderstorms 16th, and a Marginal Risk on the 17th for the Southwest and eastern portions of Central Montana.
episodes.170459: Thunderstorms moving onshore produced a strong gust along the coast in southern Brevard County.
episodes.170635: Scattered thunderstorms caused gusty outflow winds across Central and Eastern Nevada.
episodes.170666: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.170926: A thunderstorm northeast of Otter produced a severe wind gust.
episodes.170928: A north/south line of thunderstorms that stretched across multiple counties produced outflow winds well ahead of the thunderstorms. This outflow was very strong and produced winds over 60 mph. These winds produced an area of blowing dust across Interstate 90 just west of Hardin. Visibility dropped to zero resulting in a multiple car pileup which resulted in several deaths and multiple injuries.
episodes.171121: A cluster of severe thunderstorms developed across central Mississippi on the afternoon on July 14th. This cluster of storms downed several trees in the city of Kosciusko.
episodes.171332: Slow moving thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
episodes.171493: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over west central Campbell County, producing some wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.171746: Thunderstorms first developed along the sea breeze in the early afternoon hours on the southeast South Carolina coast. The thunderstorms then shifted inland along an outflow boundary and became nearly stationary across the Charleston Tri-County region. The thunderstorms repeatedly passed through an area from around Summerville and North Charleston. Extremely heavy rainfall occurred, producing flash flooding in this region. Thunderstorms also impacted the Walterboro area, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171900: It was a fairly typical summer-time regime in place with abundant moisture available and warm temperatures expected. Convergence along sea-breeze boundaries sparked off thunderstorm development. It was along these boundaries that a thunderstorm produced a waterspout and severe gusts in marine areas. The waterspout remained off-shore.
episodes.171997: Several rounds of storms with heavy rain moved across north-central Wisconsin during the early morning of July 15th. Radar estimates indicate a band of 3 to 5 inches of rain fell from northwest Clark County to the southeast part of the county. This heavy rain caused water to go over a few county roads near Chili (Clark County) and Thorp (Clark County).
episodes.172027: On July 14th, isolated thunderstorms developed in northwestern Kansas during the evening hours due to daytime heating. One of these thunderstorms became severe and produced a 60 mph wind gust which caused localized near-zero visibility due to blowing dust.
episodes.172100: The combination of CAPE, minimal SHEAR, and dew point depressions of 30-40 degrees led to a thunderstorm being able to produce severe winds.
episodes.172130: Several rounds of storms with heavy rain moved across parts of northeast Iowa during the morning of July 15th. Radar estimates indicate a band of 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across the northeast corner of Clayton County. This heavy rain pushed Bloody Run Creek out of its banks which took out a bridge in Bloody Run County Park west of Marquette (Clayton County).
episodes.172202: Thunderstorms moved through northern Wyoming as a shortwave trough crossed the area. With large dew point depressions, very strong wind gusts occurred with the high-cloud-base showers and storms. Wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph occurred across portions of Big Horn and Johnson Counties.
episodes.172364: The Atlantic high pressure ridge extended westward across Florida while a Tropical Upper Tropospheric Trough (TUTT) feature over the western Bahamas and southeast FL lifted northward. Drier air north of the TUTT advected into north central Florida through the day. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the I-75 corridor and shifted inland through the day. Thunderstorms over north central FL in the evening tapped into the drier mid-level air on the periphery of the TUTT and created an intense but highly localized downburst near the Ocala International Airport, where numerous powerlines and trees were downed.
episodes.172416: Adequate moisture and instability in place across south-central Arizona on the 14th allowed for thunderstorm development to occur across the high terrain areas of Arizona during the afternoon. Going through the evening hours, multiple outflow boundaries descended into the Valley triggering additional thunderstorm development in the lower deserts. Some of these thunderstorm became strong, including one thunderstorm that developed over the Queen Creek area, producing strong winds. As a result of the strong winds, multiple trees and power poles were knocked down in Queen Creek. No injuries were reported.
episodes.172485: A thunderstorm moved across Jo Daviess County in the early morning hours of July 15th. Lightning from this storm struck the Jo Daviess Sheriffs Office causing some damage.
episodes.172495: A combination of weak steering flow and tropical moisture resulted in slow moving thunderstorms with torrential downpours that produced a few instances of flash flooding.
episodes.172505: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots as well as a few sightings of waterspouts.
episodes.172537: A strong and persistent upper-level ridge across the Four Corners Region retrograded slightly westward, allowing an upper-level trough to shift southward from the Plains and Ozarks. The trough helped to drive a weak frontal boundary in the region where ample instability was in place as daytime maximum temperatures averaged between 100-105 degrees on July 13th. Convection began to form by mid to late afternoon with several thunderstorms quickly becoming severe in the very unstable conditions. The high-based thunderstorms presented a primary damaging wind threat, which resulted in numerous damage reports through the afternoon and evening hours on the 13th. Some of the severe thunderstorms also produced hail of various sizes, including a few reports of large hail. These storms continued through the early morning hours of the 14th before diminishing. Additional isolated severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 14th over Eastern Smith County, producing damaging winds that tore a portion of the roof off of the Chapel Hill High School cafeteria.
episodes.172592: A mid-level disturbance coupled to a cold front draped along the western Piedmont triggered scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms across the southern to northeastern Piedmont. These storms produced several reports of flash flooding in Wake and Cumberland Counties. No storms reached severe limits and the storm activity tapered off across central North Carolina by late evening.
episodes.172617: A second consecutive day of thunderstorms brought reports of significant outflow gusts.
episodes.172622: A 63 mph wind gust occurred at Monida Pass.
episodes.172657: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of the Middle Peninsula.
episodes.172660: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.172667: Thunderstorms produced damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall over Victoria. The winds blew down a tree over the road in Mission Valley and heavy rain caused flooding of streets on the northwest side of Victoria.
episodes.172691: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.172692: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.172693: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the York River.
episodes.172807: Isolated severe thunderstorms formed in eastern North Dakota during the early overnight hours, then moved into west-central Minnesota. Hail and thunderstorm wind damage were reported.
episodes.172808: Isolated severe thunderstorms formed in eastern North Dakota during the early overnight hours, then moved into west-central Minnesota. Hail and thunderstorm wind damage were reported.
episodes.172886: A push of monsoon moisture fueled an outbreak of thunderstorms across the Mojave Desert. Some storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.172905: Thunderstorm produced 1 hail near Colfax, WA.
episodes.172971: Scattered showers and thunderstorms produce isolated gale-force wind gusts as they developed along the western periphery of an upper level low pressure system, with an inverted lower tropospheric trough.
episodes.173025: A stalled front across Pitt County on the evening of July 14th allowed multiple rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms to move over the same area during the evening.  With a very moist atmosphere in place, localized heavy rain over the City of Greenville caused flash flooding throughout the city.  Multiple water rescues occurred due to cars stranded in water. The hardest hit area was Downtown Greenville.
episodes.173026: An area of heavy rain and thunderstorms moved over the same area of Pamlico County on the morning of July 15th to produce flash flooding near Merritt. The previous night a similar pattern produced flash flooding in Greenville.

Around 4:15 PM MDT, a thunderstorm outflow moved through the Hardin area. It produced a wind gust of 62 mph in the 4:35 PM MDT observations from the Big Horn County Airport. Along with the outflow winds, blowing dust reduced visibility to less than a quarter mile on the AWOS. This resulted in a 20 to 30 vehicle pile up along Interstate 90 around mile marker 493 reported at 4:30 PM MDT, very close to the airport. Prior to this, the Montana DOT RWIS station at Arrow Creek Hill, 25 miles west of Hardin, reported a peak wind gust of 48 mph about 15 minutes prior. This accident resulted in 6 deaths and multiple injuries.
